The case ran in a few white papers in Maryland, West Virginia and New York, which treated it chiefly as a scandal of interracial "depravity".

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of John Clements
episodes.lead: The attempted lynching of John Clements took place at West Point, King William County, Virginia, on the night of December 12, 1903, when white residents seized Clements, a Black man accused of shooting the white dairyman George Hobough, and, by one account, put a rope around his neck. He was handed to officers, and Hobough died in a Richmond hospital on December 23. Convicted of first-degree murder, Clements was legally hanged on March 11, 1904, an execution wire reports noted mainly for his baptism in the box that carried his body to a medical college.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of John Haynes
episodes.lead: The attempted lynching of John Haynes took place in December 1903, when mobs twice tried to take Haynes, a sixteen-year-old Black youth accused of attempted assault, from jail in Madison County, Tennessee. Early on December 6 a crowd of 'men and boys' tried to break into the county jail at Jackson but was turned back by the sheriff and dispersed by police, and days later a mob broke open the jail at Henderson but did not find him. Haynes was later tried at Jackson and sentenced to twenty-one years in the penitentiary.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of John Revel
episodes.lead: The attempted lynching of John Revel happened at Twenty-eighth Street and Eighth Avenue in New York City early on a Saturday in December 1903, when a crowd tried to take Revel, described as 'a young negro', from police officers and hang him to a lamp-post. The police drew their revolvers and the crowd gave way, and Revel was taken off by his captors. The episode ran as a wire item under the headline 'Attempt to Lynch Negro in New York' and was notable as a lynching attempt in a Northern city.

episodes.title: Lynching of Lewis Jackson
episodes.lead: The lynching of Lewis Jackson was the hanging of a Black man by white men near Tampa, Florida, on the night of December 4, 1903, shortly after the sheriff released him from jail. Jackson had been accused of an assault on the three- or four-year-old daughter of R. F. Ensey of the government works at the entrance to Tampa Bay, and the papers said he was freed because no state law covered the offense. The wire report said a mob of fifty white men hanged him, while special telegrams to New York papers described two or three successive mobs, one of which mutilated him before another hanged him.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of the Pembroke prisoners
episodes.lead: The threatened lynching of the Pembroke prisoners took place in December 1903 in Christian County, Kentucky, when nine Black men held in the Hopkinsville jail, accused of murdering a white stranger near Pembroke, were moved by night to Madisonville after reports that a mob would take them. No attack on the jail was reported, and by the end of January 1904 three of the nine were under sentence of death. An Associated Press dispatch spread the story nationally, while the local Hopkinsville Kentuckian doubted that a mob had been a real danger.

episodes.title: Threatened lynching of Black prisoners at Shawnee, Oklahoma Territory
episodes.lead: The threatened lynching of Black prisoners at Shawnee, Oklahoma Territory, occurred on the evening of December 16, 1903, when citizens resolved to take "summary vengeance" on Black men arrested for a murder in the railroad yards. The sheriff and his deputies moved the prisoners to Tecumseh before dark, and no violence was reported.

episodes.title: Killing of T. J. Thomas
episodes.lead: The killing of T. J. Thomas was the fatal shooting of a Black man by Mounted Policeman Jesse F. Greek at Jacksonville on the night of Wednesday, December 9, 1903. According to the only report found, Greek fired after Thomas came at him with an open razor during a quarrel, and the story ran as a brief item in the Savannah Morning News two days later.

episodes.title: Attempted lynching of Wade Bennett
episodes.lead: The attempted lynching of Wade Bennett took place on the night of Monday, December 14, 1903, when an armed mob surrounded the jail at Clayton, Georgia, intending to lynch Bennett, a Black man accused of fatally shooting a white railroad construction boss, Frank Lesuer. The jailor slipped Bennett out of the jail to a private home, where he was guarded until the mob dispersed. Only the Savannah Morning News reported the mob; other white papers carried the shooting under the headline "Lesuer Killed by Negro" without mentioning it.
